judge_output.rationale: Zuckerman (2022MNRAS.514..227Z) already used Spitzer and WISE infrared data to constrain the frequency of Dyson-sphere-like structures at white dwarfs, which is a closely related claim tested with broadband photometry. Murillo-Ojeda et al. (2026A&A...707A.268M) built the 100 pc Gaia white dwarf infrared-excess catalogue (456 sources) that defines the card's parent sample, but interprets the excesses only as disks or companions. Owens et al. (2023AJ....166....5O) and Lai et al. (2021ApJ...920..156L) show disk/companion separation by near-IR spectroscopy or photometry for small samples, and Owens leaves one excess unexplained. No listed work classifies the 100 pc excess population with 1-5 um spectral band depths plus metal-pollution checks to look for a featureless 250-500 K group, which is what SPHEREx would add.

closest_prior.relation: Constrains the frequency of Dyson-sphere structures at white dwarfs with Spitzer/WISE/TESS/Kepler photometry; same hypothesis, but no SPHEREx 1-5 um spectral classification of the 100 pc sample.

Complete 100 pc Gaia white dwarf infrared-excess catalogue from VOSA SED fits with WISE/2MASS photometry; same sample but attributes excesses to disks or companions without band-depth classification or a search for featureless cool non-polluted excesses.
Near-IR spectroscopy separates disks from brown dwarf companions in seven white dwarfs and leaves one excess (Gaia J0723+6301) unexplained; the same spectral-feature logic, applied to a tiny sample.
Spitzer/Gemini follow-up of Gaia+unWISE excess candidates with a photometric method to separate companions from dust disks; broadband only, no technosignature-motivated third class.

judge_output.what_would_make_it_open: No listed work uses SPHEREx R~35-130 spectra of the 100 pc white dwarf excess sample, combined with spectroscopic metal-pollution checks, to test whether a featureless 250-500 K excess population exists beyond disks and companions.

judge_output.rationale: The card's measured quantity is the spectral shape of the 1-5 um excess around 100 pc Gaia white dwarfs: a fitted excess temperature plus band depths at 1.4, 1.9, 3.3 and 4.6 um from SPHEREx low-resolution spectra, used to separate featureless ~300 K excesses from debris disks and molecular-band companions. Prior white-dwarf excess surveys (Murillo-Ojeda 2026, Lai 2021, Wang 2023/2026) and the white-dwarf Dyson-sphere constraint of Zuckerman 2022 rest on broadband WISE/Spitzer/2MASS photometry. Broadband photometry can show that an excess exists and give a rough temperature, but it cannot measure molecular band depths or show that a spectrum is featureless. Owens 2023 took near-infrared spectra of only seven systems, and no listed work applies SPHEREx spectra to white dwarfs, so the claim of no third featureless group is untested.

closest_prior.relation: constrains the frequency of Dyson-sphere-like structures at white dwarfs using Spitzer/WISE photometry and TESS/Kepler optical data, without 1-5 um spectral band depths to separate featureless excesses from companions.

builds the complete 100 pc Gaia white dwarf infrared-excess catalogue from VOSA SED fits to broadband photometry, which classifies disks and companions without molecular band measurements and with no search for featureless cool excesses.
uses near-infrared spectroscopy to tell disks from L-dwarf companions in seven white dwarfs and leaves one excess unexplained, a small targeted sample rather than an all-sky spectral classification.
confirms unWISE excesses with Spitzer 3.6/4.5 um and JHK photometry and separates companions from disks by colours, not by spectral features.
